Tourism revenue is called 'invisible exports'. Why?
Funds come in but nothing leaves the country
The money is not recorded by government
Tourists do not pay any taxes
Goods are sent out without being seen
Tourism revenue is called invisible exports because funds come in but nothing leaves the country.
Tourism is Botswana's second largest revenue earner after:
Tourism is the second largest revenue earner for Botswana after diamond mining.
What share of Botswana's GDP does tourism provide?
Tourism is responsible for 12% of the Gross Domestic Product (GDP).
What percentage of all employment in Botswana does tourism provide?
Tourism provides 8% of all employment in Botswana.
Where does Botswana rank in Africa by tourist numbers?
1st, with about 10 million tourists a year
2nd, with about 8 million tourists a year
8th, with about 1 million tourists a year
Botswana is ranked 12 with 850 000 tourists per year, growing by about 8.5% a year.
What has always been Botswana's tourism policy?
Botswana's policy of 'high financial yield, low impact' means an expensive destination with low capacity.
How does Botswana's tourism compare with Namibia's?
Fewer tourists, but higher total revenue
More tourists and higher total revenue
More tourists, but lower total revenue
Fewer tourists and lower total revenue
Despite tourism numbers being lower than Namibia, Botswana's total revenue from tourism is higher.
Why does tourism not have a limited life-span like mining?
It is run by the government
Tourism, being non-consumptive, does not have a limited life-span in the way mining does.
How does tourism help families in rural areas?
People need not leave their families to find city work
It moves rural families into the big cities
It replaces the need for schools in villages
It provides free housing in Gaborone
Tourism brings wealth to outlying areas, so Batswana are not forced to leave their families to look for work in cities.
Which traditional skills has the guiding profession given value to?
Tracking and trapping animals, gathering wild foods
Guiding has given value to skills like tracking and trapping of animals for food and gathering natural foods.
What percentage of Botswana is set aside as wildlife management areas?
17% of Botswana is game reserves and national parks and a further 10% is wildlife management areas.
Which of these does the manual list as an environmental impact of tourism?
Clearing land and importing soil for airstrips
Game-drive roads, off-road driving and clearing areas and importing soil for airstrips all cause disturbance.
How does the physical process of tourism start?
Buying food and beverage for lodges
It starts with promoting Botswana as a wildlife destination through travel fairs, road-shows and documentaries.
Foreign travel agents who lack local knowledge often book through a:
Many foreign agents book through a Destination Management Company or local travel agency that specialises in the region.
What should hands be washed with before preparing food?
When preparing food, hands should be washed with an anti-bacterial soap.
What should be done with cracked or chipped crockery and glasses?
They should be used for staff only
They should be glued and reused
They should be kept for sundowners
The manual states that cracked or chipped crockery and glasses should be destroyed.
Why should food be served either hot or cold?
Guests prefer food straight from the pan
Cold food is cheaper to prepare
Bacteria breed at mid-range temperatures, so foods like fish, chicken and dairy can quickly become dangerous.
What percentage of Botswana's land is set aside as protected areas?
Botswana has set aside 45% of its land area as protected areas.
How much of Botswana is freehold land?
Only 6% of Botswana is freehold land, such as Ghanzi, Tuli and Pandamatenga; most is tribal land.
Under the 1975 Tribal Land Grazing Policy, which type of grazing land was the largest?
The TLGP divided grazing land into commercial, communal (the largest) and reserved (for later use).
In which schedule of the Wildlife Conservation and National Parks Act are national parks specified?
National parks are specified in the first schedule and have the highest level of protection.
By what time must approved night drives in national parks return to the facility?
The Act provides for approved night drives with a professional guide, returning by 22:00 (none are currently approved).
What are the summer opening and closing times for national parks and game reserves?
Summer times are 05:30-19:00 and winter times are 06:30-18:30.
Which area of Chobe National Park is renowned as one of Africa's best areas for predators?
Savuti is renowned as one of the best areas in Africa for predators; the riverfront is famous for elephant.
Baines' Baobabs were made famous when Thomas Baines painted them in:
Baines' Baobabs were painted by Thomas Baines on an expedition in 1862.
Makgadikgadi Pans National Park was established to protect which salt pans?
Makgadikgadi Pans National Park was established to protect the massive Sua and Ntwetwe salt pans.
On what type of land are game reserves found, compared with national parks?
Game reserves on tribal land; parks on state land
Game reserves on state land; parks on tribal land
Both are on communal grazing land
Game reserves are on tribal land whereas national parks are on state land.
Mannyelanong Game Reserve was declared to protect which species?
Some game reserves protect specific species, such as Mannyelanong for the Cape griffon.
What is the penalty for illegal hunting or capture of animals in a game reserve?
Up to P5 000 or 5 years in prison
Up to P10 000 or 7 years in prison
Up to P100 000 or 15 years in prison
A warning on the first offence
Illegal hunting or capture attracts fines of up to P5 000 or 5 years, while off-road driving first attracts a warning.
Which island in Moremi Game Reserve has no public vehicle access?
Chief's Island has two lodges and there is no public access by vehicle to the island.
In which year was the Central Kalahari Game Reserve established?
The CKGR, covering about 52,800 km², was established in 1961.
Which sanctuary was declared mainly to protect rhino?
Sanctuaries are often declared for a specific species, such as rhino at Khama Rhino Sanctuary.
Nata Sanctuary is one of only how many breeding sites for lesser flamingo?
Nata Sanctuary was established to protect the flamingo and is one of only 5 breeding sites for lesser flamingo.
In which schedule of the Act are Wildlife Management Areas specified?
WMAs are specified in the third schedule of the Wildlife Conservation and National Parks Act.
How do WMAs acting as 'buffers' help protected areas?
They keep the human edge effect out of core areas
They allow off-road driving next to parks
They keep tourists out of national parks
They stop all animal movement between parks
Buffers restrict the edge effect of human/wildlife conflict to the buffer areas and not the core conservation areas.
How many scheduled Controlled Hunting Areas are there?
There are 40 scheduled CHAs, specified in the fourth schedule of the Act.
Which type of CHA is strictly photographic, community-run and usually next to core conservation areas?
Community photographic areas are owned and operated by communities and usually adjacent to core conservation areas.
What is a commercial multi-purpose CHA?
Like community multi-purpose but leased by a company
Strictly photographic and owned by the state
A hunting area only for citizens
A photographic area run by the community
Commercial multi-purpose is as per community multi-purpose but leased by a company.
How are Controlled Hunting Areas named?
With a district prefix and a number, e.g. KD 1
With the name of the lodge that leases them
With a number only, from 1 to 40
Areas are named with a prefix according to the district and numbered, e.g. KD 1, KD 2 in the Kgalagadi.
Who issues hunting quotas for each WMA?
Department of Wildlife and National Parks
The Department of Wildlife and National Parks issues quotas; part is commercial and the rest is for citizen hunting for meat.
Botswana's only transfrontier park, Kgalagadi, stretches into which country?
Botswana currently has only 1 transfrontier park, the Kgalagadi Transfrontier Park, which stretches into South Africa.
Which countries are included in the intended KAZA-TFCA?
Botswana, South Africa, Namibia, Lesotho, Zambia
KAZA includes land of Botswana, Zambia, Angola, Namibia and Zimbabwe.
In what year was the Okavango registered as a UNESCO World Heritage Site?
The Okavango was registered as a natural site in 2014 and was the 1000th site registered with UNESCO.
Under which category is Tsodilo Hills registered with UNESCO?
Tsodilo Hills is registered as a cultural site, while the Okavango is a natural site.
About how many San paintings are protected at Tsodilo Hills?
The UNESCO World Heritage Site protects an estimated 4,500 San paintings.
What are the 3 main hills at Tsodilo called?
The site consists of 3 main hills, the male, female and child, plus a 4th unnamed hill.
Why are the Gcwihaba and Aha Hills riddled with caves?
They were dug out by miners
These hills are riddled with caves because the principal rock is dolomite.
Drotsky's Cave is famous for its:
The caves are famous for the thousands of bats that roost in the caverns.
The Makgadikgadi Pans are a remnant of which ancient lake?
The pans are a remnant of Paleo Lake Makgadikgadi, which covered over 100,000 km² in northern Botswana.
A rocky outcrop in the pans covered in baobabs
An island in the Okavango with two lodges
A sandbank in the Chobe River
A hill at Tsodilo with San paintings
Kubu Island is a dramatic rocky outcrop in the pans covered in baobab trees and is popular for camping.
Why can Nata Sanctuary offer spectacular flamingo viewing?
It is the last part of Sua Pan to dry up
It is the deepest part of Ntwetwe Pan
It has the most baobab trees
It is fed by the Boteti River all year
As the last part of Sua Pan to dry up, Nata can give some of the most spectacular flamingo viewing in the country.
Where is most of the wildlife found in Nxai Pan National Park?
North of the baobabs on the vegetated Nxai Pan
Around Baines' Baobabs on the rocky ridge
On the open salt pan surface
Most of the wildlife is north of the baobabs on the vegetated Nxai Pan, making it more popular with tourists.
Which of these is a protected mammal in Botswana?
Klipspringer is on the list of protected mammals; the others are not listed.
Which of these birds is protected in Botswana?
Kori bustard is on the protected birds list, along with Stanley's bustard and others.
What is currently the only protected reptile in Botswana?
Currently the only protected reptile in Botswana is the African rock python.
What is the maximum penalty for illegally killing a rhinoceros?
P100 000 fine or 15 years in prison
P10 000 fine or 7 years in prison
P5 000 fine or 5 years in prison
P50 000 fine or 10 years in prison
For other protected animals the penalty is up to P10 000 or 7 years; for rhino it is P100 000 or 15 years.
Why are wild dog the most difficult protected species to manage?
Their huge home ranges bring them into conflict
They only live inside national parks
They are hunted for their skins
Their massive home ranges bring them into conflict with farmers and domestic dogs that carry canine distemper.
Species with the highest CITES protection (absolutely zero trade) are listed on:
Appendix 1 gives the highest protection (zero trade) and Appendix 3 the lowest (limited, controlled trade).
What is the aim of CITES?
To stop international trade threatening species
To set national park entry fees
To control hunting quotas in WMAs
CITES aims to ensure that international trade in wild animals and plants does not threaten their survival.
In which year was the Tourism Act designed?
The Botswana Government designed the Tourism Act in 1992 to regulate the growth and development of tourism.
Why is the wet season (November to March) the best time for birdwatchers?
The roads are easiest to drive
The wet season is best for birdwatchers due to the influx of migratory species.
When is prime game viewing considered to be?
Prime game viewing is September to late November, depending on the onset of rains.
Which months does the manual say are the most moderate for temperature?
As far as temperature is concerned, April/May and August are the most moderate months.
